chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib ibn Usman, from Rawh ibn Abd al-Rahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about buying the parchments (copies of the Quran) and selling them, so he said: 'The paper was only placed by the pulpit, and the space between the pulpit and the wall was the measure of what a sheep could pass through, or a man walking sideways.' He said: 'The man would come and write from that, then indeed they would sell it after that.' I said, 'So what do you think regarding that?' He said to me, 'Buying is more beloved to me than if I were to sell it.' I said, 'So what do you think if I were to give a recompense for its writing?' He said, 'There is no problem, but this is how they were doing (in those days).'

key_terms.الْمَصَاحِفِ: Parchments or copies of the Quran

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay someone for copying the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the early practical method of Quranic reproduction, where scribes copied text from sheets placed near the pulpit (minbar) in the mosque, reflecting a time when standardized books were not yet ubiquitous. The Imam’s preference for buying over selling and his permission of a wage (ujra) for the scribe’s labor underscore the distinction between the sacred text itself and the human effort of transcription, a key principle in Shia fiqh regarding the sanctity of the Quranic parchment.
